For NextItNet, test causality by holding the prefix through position t fixed, perturbing only future nonpadding embeddings, and comparing features through t in evaluation mode. As a positive control, deliberately inject an actual future dependency: capture the current forward’s embedding at j>t and add a scaled copy to the hooked output at t. A constant perturbation independent of the changed embedding cannot validate detection of future dependence. Preserve the residual mapping F(x)+x: add the injected signal to the existing output, rather than replacing the block with its convolution branch. These are test-design recommendations derived from [NextItNet’s residual architecture](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf).

Use module-local forward hooks; clone the output before editing and return the modified clone. Clone captured observations too, preventing subsequent in-place operations from changing them. Track every temporary handle and call handle.remove() in try/finally, including when forward raises; always_call=True does not automatically remove hooks. Snapshot each module’s training flag and all registered buffers, including nonpersistent buffers; restore buffers under no_grad and restore flags individually, preserving mixed train/eval modes. A shallow state_dict snapshot is insufficient because its tensors reference live state and exclude nonpersistent buffers. See [PyTorch Module documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.Module.html).

Run probes on cached, cloned batches or deterministic histories with private RNGs. Avoid creating or advancing the training DataLoader iterator: sampling, worker startup and prefetching can advance sampler or worker RNG state. Restoring the main process RNG cannot rewind worker processes. Preserve Python/NumPy RNGs and use torch.random.fork_rng for CPU and relevant CUDA RNG state; it does not cover separate generators. See [DataLoader documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/data.html) and [PyTorch RNG documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/random.html).
